headline: SDF Ends Its Independent Command
deck: Mazloum Abdi announced the end of the SDF’s mission and its dissolution as an independent military force after integration into Syrian Army brigades. President Ahmad al-Sharaa received him the same evening. No unit roster, payroll or weapons inventory was published.
body: Mazloum Abdi said in Damascus on 25 August that the Syrian Democratic Forces had completed integration into brigades of the Syrian Army and were dissolving as an independent military force [E1][E3]. SANA put the announcement at 10:14 p.m. local time, 19:14 UTC [E1]. Hawar News carried the same core line: the end of the SDF’s mission and, with full responsibility, its dissolution as an independent military force [E3]. Dissolve applies to the independent organisation. Integrate applies to the claimed transfer into army brigades [E1][E3].

President Ahmad al-Sharaa received Abdi and his delegation at the People’s Palace the same evening, with Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani and Deir Ezzor Governor Ziad al-Ayesh present [E2]. SANA timestamped that notice at 10:28 p.m. local, 19:28 UTC [E2]. The presidency item listed integration into state institutions, steps for the next phase, and strengthening state presence [E2]. SANA framed the move as placing security and military responsibilities under official state institutions and a single national chain of command [E1].

What did not print is the operating ledger. The 25 August communiqués name no formations, no new commanders, no payroll, no heavy-weapons schedule, no detention sites, no oil fields and no border crossings [E1][E2][E3]. Full integration is a high-level announcement without a unit roster [E1][E3]. Parallel administrative structures are asserted as ending; Kurdish civil institutions are not inventoried [E1].
No CENTCOM or Pentagon primary statement was located by the freeze [E1][E2]. Whether Syria names at least one former SDF formation and its new command by 1 September is the next public test [E1][E2].
